title: Pods pinned to capacity-type on-demand cannot use reserved capacity

detection.reason: read from Pod rows as key=value pairs — nodeSelector is collected per pod, and node affinity is not scanned, so a clean result here does not clear an affinity term

quote: With the `ReservedCapacity` feature flag, Karpenter introduces a new `karpenter.sh/capacity-type` value (`reserved`). This means any applications that explicitly select on `on-demand` with a `nodeSelector` and want to utilize ODCR capacity may need to update their requirements to use `nodeAffinity` to opt-in to using both `reserved` and `on-demand` capacity.
remediation: Only relevant if you enable the `ReservedCapacity` feature gate and use ODCR capacity. These pods select `capacity-type=on-demand` with a nodeSelector, which cannot express two values; rewrite them as a `nodeAffinity` term listing both `reserved` and `on-demand` so they can land on either.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.nodeSelector["karpenter.sh/capacity-type"] == "on-demand") | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each pod printed can never schedule onto reserved capacity while it uses a nodeSelector
